Specification: This specification models a reconfigurable Paxos-style consensus algorithm with acceptors casting votes across instances and ballots, and with reconfiguration commands that change the active configuration. The state consists of per-acceptor votes `avote` and a set `learned` of learned instance-command pairs; the spec defines when votes are cast, when an acceptor abstains, when a value is learned, and how configurations are derived from learned reconfiguration commands. The file proves safety properties only, not liveness: it states the standard temporal specification `Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<avote, learned>>`, proves type correctness and a safety invariant, and then develops a substantial TLAPS proof showing an inductive invariant for reconfiguration safety.

             CONSTANT c \in Cmd
      PROVE Stable( /\ Voted(a, i, b, C.cnum, c)
                    /\ ConfigOKAt(i, b, C)  )

SUFFICES ASSUME Next, Voted(a, i, b, C.cnum, c),

                 PROVE  ConfigOKAt(i, b, C)'

                      CONSTANT c1 \in Cmd,
                      CONSTANT c2 \in Cmd,
                      <<i, c1>> \in learned /\ <<i, c2>> \in learned
               PROVE  c1 = c2

                 C # cfgC[ Max({j \in 0..maxcfg : cfgi[j] < i}) ]

The unnamed theorems `Spec => []TypeOK` and `Spec => []SafetyInv`, and the theorem name entry `Inv => SafetyInv`, are theorem statements rather than operator definitions; only defined operators are partitioned here.

Inv is classified as a state predicate because it is Boolean-valued and contains no primed variables or explicit temporal operators; apostrophized references to subexpressions such as `Inv!1'` occur only in proofs and do not make the operator definition temporal.

Config, Vote, and the two record-set expressions written with colon syntax are included in FunctionConstructor_SetType because they are `[S -> T]`-style set-of-functions/records forms rather than by-domain `|->` constructors.
All UnchangedExprs entries are simple variable references (`UNCHANGED learned`, `UNCHANGED avote`); there are no `UNCHANGED <<...>>` forms in this file.
